en.def: Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Fetch relevant documents at query time and stuff them into the model's prompt before generation. Reduces hallucination at the cost of latency and prompt-budget complexity.
Splitting text into discrete units (tokens) that the model processes. Typical tokens are subword fragments — a token is roughly 3–4 characters in English.

Server-side reuse of compute for a prompt prefix. Sending the same prefix in multiple requests within a TTL reuses the cached KV state, dropping latency and cost. Anthropic's cache TTL is 5 minutes by default.
Maximum number of tokens the model can consider at once. Includes both input and output.
Fixed-dimensional vector representation of text such that semantically similar text has similar vectors. Used for retrieval, clustering, similarity search.
Database optimized for nearest-neighbour search over high-dimensional vectors. Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector, Qdrant are common.
Model emits a structured tool invocation that the host runtime executes; the result feeds back into the model's context. The basis for agent loops.
Plausible-sounding output that's factually wrong. The model has no built-in distinction between recalled fact and confident fabrication.
Including a small number of input/output examples in the prompt to demonstrate the desired pattern. Cheap form of in-context learning.
Sampling parameters. Top-k = sample from the k most likely next tokens. Top-p (nucleus) = sample from the smallest token set whose cumulative probability ≥ p.
